title: BBC Ghosts from the Past
paragraphs: A BBC supernatural-drama collection of ghost stories dramatized for radio, presented here as a small group of eerie standalone plays.
Four-part BBC Radio 4 supernatural-drama anthology directed by Martin Jenkins.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: BBC Radio 4 April 1992 run (April 8, 1992 to April 29, 1992) on [[org|org.deepv2.507b7f3aadcb7123|BBC Radio 4]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Martin Jenkins (director), Brett Usher (performer), David Learner (performer), Eric Allan (performer), Gudrun Ure (performer), Ann Windsor (performer), and Benjamin Whitrow (performer).

The stories often return to ghosts and supernatural haunting, memory, guilt and the return of the past, M. R. James and antiquarian ghost-story tradition, marriage, death and obsessive possession, and Oxbridge academic supernatural setting.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes BBC Radio 4 Ghosts from the Past run and Modern BBC revival of the literary ghost-play tradition.
plain_text:
A BBC supernatural-drama collection of ghost stories dramatized for radio, presented here as a small group of eerie standalone plays.

Four-part BBC Radio 4 supernatural-drama anthology directed by Martin Jenkins.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: BBC Radio 4 April 1992 run (April 8, 1992 to April 29, 1992) on BBC Radio 4.

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Martin Jenkins (director), Brett Usher (performer), David Learner (performer), Eric Allan (performer), Gudrun Ure (performer), Ann Windsor (performer), and Benjamin Whitrow (performer).

The stories often return to ghosts and supernatural haunting, memory, guilt and the return of the past, M. R. James and antiquarian ghost-story tradition, marriage, death and obsessive possession, and Oxbridge academic supernatural setting.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes BBC Radio 4 Ghosts from the Past run and Modern BBC revival of the literary ghost-play tradition.
